title: Regularization of Vortex Core Size in Photon BECs due to Harmonic Trap: An Analytical Approach
authors: Joshua Krauß, Tabitha Bates, Francisco Ednilson Alves dos Santos, Axel Pelster
abstract: Quantized vortices are a hallmark of superfluidity. However, in a photon Bose--Einstein condensate, the photon-photon interaction is so weak that in a homogeneous system the healing length exceeds the experimentally achievable size of the condensate itself. Here we show that a harmonic confinement regularizes the vortex size to experimentally achievable scales. Moreover, such an external confinement closely resembles the standard experimental setup of a pumped dye-filled microcavity. We model the condensate via a complex Gross--Pitaevskii equation and obtain an approximate dynamical single-vortex solution by applying the recently proposed projection optimization method. The latter generalizes the variational approach of closed systems to open-dissipative systems without assuming a specific form for the condensate phase. The radial photon flow, which is characteristic for driven-dissipative systems, yields a definition of the vortex core size based on the competition of gain and loss. However, this condition reproduces the heuristic closed system definition now based on physical grounds. A subsequent linear stability analysis shows that interaction, as well as pumping and loss can drive the system to an unstable regime. In this way one can fundamentally distinguish between closed and open-dissipative systems.
summary: This paper analytically investigates how harmonic trapping regularizes the unphysical vortex core size in photon BECs. Using the complex Gross-Pitaevskii equation and the projection optimization method, the authors derive physical conditions for vortex stability. The work provides a rigorous framework to distinguish between closed and open-dissipative quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the issue of vortex core size regularization in Photon Bose-Einstein Condensates (BECs) where weak interactions cause the healing length to exceed the condensate size in homogeneous systems.
main_result: Harmonic confinement regularizes the vortex core size to experimentally achievable scales, and the analysis fundamentally distinguishes between closed and open-dissipative quantum systems.
method: The authors employ the projection optimization method to solve the complex Gross-Pitaevskii equation (cGPE) for open-dissipative systems, followed by linear stability analysis.
model_or_system: The system models a photon BEC in a dye-filled microcavity, governed by a complex Gross-Pitaevskii equation that includes terms for pumping ($\gamma$) and density-dependent losses ($\Gamma$).
key_observables: Vortex core size, radial velocity component ($v_R$), condensate width ($q$), and the breathing mode frequency ($\omega_{breath}$).
important_parameters: Pumping strength ($\gamma$), loss rate ($\Gamma$), interaction strength ($g$), and the harmonic trap frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the projection optimization method for open-dissipative systems and assumes radial symmetry for the hydrodynamic description.
figures_summary: Figures compare projection optimization parameters for vortex-free vs. vortex states, show the stability eigenvalues ($\lambda$) dependence on pumping/loss ratios, and illustrate the spatial separation of gain/loss regions and the sign change of the integrated particle flux.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the cGPE and the projection optimization method to find approximate solutions. It then analyzes the steady-state vortex and vortex-free solutions, followed by a linear stability analysis to determine the system's dynamical regimes and distinguish between open and closed systems.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it applies advanced techniques (projection optimization) to model non-equilibrium, open quantum systems, providing physical insights into topological defects (vortices) in quantum optics platforms.
